rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_HTTPS_Profile {
    meta:
        description = "Detects Cobalt Strike beaconing over HTTPS based on JA3 fingerprint and URI patterns"
        author = "SOC Threat Intel Team"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $s1 = "GET /static/" nocase
        $s2 = "Accept: */*" nocase
        $s3 = "Cache-Control: no-cache" nocase
        $j1 = { 7F 45 4C 46 02 01 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 02 00 3E 00 } // ELF header
    condition:
        all of ($s*) and $j1 at 0
}

arguments.summary: A phishing-initiated ransomware attack was detected and contained following a Cobalt Strike beacon deployment on workstation WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42). The attacker gained initial access via a malicious email triggering an encoded PowerShell download. The payload, identified as CobaltStrike.Beacon (SHA256: a1b2c3d4e5f6...), established C2 communication, performed host reconnaissance, and attempted lateral movement via SMB. The threat was contained by isolating the host and blocking C2 traffic. No ransomware encryption occurred due to timely detection and response. Domain controller (10.0.1.50) was not compromised.

Host WS-FIN-042 isolated from network and C2 IPs blocked at firewall.
Beacon.dll quarantined, persistence mechanisms removed, full EDR scan completed.
Incident declared contained. Recovery and validation initiated.

        $http_post = /POST \/[a-z]{4}\// nocase
        $user_agent = "Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1;" fullword ascii
        $x86_header = { 55 8B EC 83 EC 10 53 56 57 } // Common x86 function prologue

    condition:
        (2 of ($http_*) or $user_agent) and $x86_header
}
